extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. It combines diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets plus 3 newly created datasets, and supports fine-grained evaluation with metadata annotations.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled by collecting and consolidating existing multimodal MathQA and VQA datasets, automatically filtering math-related VQA examples with heuristic rules, manually labeling them with expert annotators and majority voting, and creating three new datasets with manual annotation and review by graduate students.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data included 28 existing multimodal datasets (nine MathQA and 19 VQA datasets), plus newly sourced puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations such as tables, figures, and charts from online education resources and papers on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 2023 for the PaperQA source papers
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For filtering VQA examples, three expert annotators manually labeled whether each example involved mathematical reasoning using a custom annotation tool. Annotators were trained with detailed instructions and examples, and could choose Yes/No/Unsure. Final labels used majority voting. For three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields; each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and disagreements were resolved through discussion to reach consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool / GUI; Amazon Mechanical Turk (for the human performance study).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was analyzed using Fleiss Kappa among three annotators for mathematical-reasoning labels, yielding 0.775. For the newly collected datasets, independent annotation by three reviewers achieved 99.2% inter-annotation consistency, with only 6 of 736 questions showing disagreements; these were resolved by team discussion.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotations per item for the mathematical-reasoning labeling and for the newly collected datasets; five annotators per question in the AMT human performance study.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Expert annotators; graduate students in STEM fields. For the AMT study, annotators had completed more than 5,000 HIT tasks and had an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic automatic filtering rules were used to preselect likely math-related VQA examples, selecting examples with numeric answers or quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has incomplete coverage of mathematical problems and visual contexts, may not generalize well to other domains, requires labor-intensive collection for high-quality data, has annotations for only 85.6% of examples, uses heterogeneous non-unified annotation formats, and may contain data noise. It also notes model evaluation was limited to recent prominent models and that OCR/object recognition weaknesses can hinder performance on natural-image questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the benchmark as enabling AI systems with mathematical reasoning in visual contexts for real-world applications in education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Grade level is included as metadata annotation for examples.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark to facilitate development and fine-grained evaluation of mathematical reasoning systems in visual contexts, especially for assessing LLMs and LMMs on tasks such as figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problems, textbook question answering, and visual question answering.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is described as an ongoing research effort; the authors plan future iterations with broader problem and visual coverage, unified annotations, refinement of data noise based on community feedback, and updates to the leaderboard as new models emerge.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Created a testmini subset by randomly sampling examples from each source dataset: first sampling up to a threshold of 4 questions per source dataset, then sampling remaining questions proportionally to each source dataset's share in the full set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Conducted quality checks to identify and address errors in the dataset.
